long_biography.plain_text:
Main Street in Rockville brought Scott Copeland's property experience into a community he created with his wife, Jillian. It combines affordable apartments with shared spaces and activities for adults of different abilities. His development team manages the apartments, while Main Street Connect organises the programmes. Membership also extends to people who live elsewhere, allowing the community to reach beyond the building's residents.

Copeland acquired Bethesda Magazine and Bethesda Beat from Susan and Steve Hull in 2021, entering local news publishing. He sold the magazine and its companion news website, renamed MoCo360, to Today Media in 2024. Both publications continued to operate locally within the new owner's wider regional publishing business.

confidence.reason: The founders' public interview describes the programme/apartment distinction and wider membership; the organisation and later county decision corroborate the completed community. WTOP directly documents both publishing acquisition and sale, with local operations continuing.

uncertainties: Exact-input inventory preceded full-name Forbes-first searching. The explicit NTSB legal-name statement and the county's exact full-name business record resolve identity; the Why Not/Lovebug specifications provide a distinctive bridge. Unrelated authors, photographers, contractors, athletes and other Michael Scott Copeland namesakes were excluded.

No standalone personal Forbes profile was found. Searches covered full and professional names, LinkedIn, Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube, TikTok and Wikipedia with RST, Main Street, Jillian and publishing qualifiers. Organisation posts and interview videos do not qualify as personal accounts. TikTok access was restricted; no verified account was established there. Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow supplied no demonstrated relevant personal account.

The LinkedIn account is proposed using two directly inspected professional links from independent publishing and community contexts. Its own activity is not treated as independent corroboration. RST's company website remains unverified because retrieval failed.

Birth date and birthplace remain blank: no directly inspected dependable source gives them. No middle-name change, secondary nationality, title, suffix or secondary residence is supported. An inaccessible Florida Housing underwriting PDF is a discovery lead only; indexed education and ownership figures were not adopted.

The family partnership and operating expansion support broad Self-made. Father's co-founding does not by itself establish inherited wealth, a gift, or a materially advantaged launch. The financing and predecessor circumstances remain insufficient for a narrower origin category.

RST's continuing operating mandate supports Real Estate as current principal industry. Its gross property portfolio and company project values are not personal net worth. The 2024 publishing sale rules out a current publishing CEO or ownership claim; no exact current private asset allocation is asserted.

Main Street's initial interview described an emerging project, while the organisation and October 2025 county decision confirm the completed community. Programme membership and apartment management are distinct; no unsupported claim of medical treatment, care outcomes or private family health history appears.

Residential development is the minimum useful active tag. A relatively brief publishing ownership period and community contribution do not automatically justify separate industry or generic philanthropy tags. No formal taxonomy candidate is created.
